chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him mercy) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Fudayl ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'He is the First and the Last,' and I said: 'As for the First, we have understood it, but as for the Last, explain its interpretation to us.' He said: 'There is nothing except that it perishes or changes, or enters into alteration and decay, or transitions from one color to another, from one form to another, from one attribute to another, from increase to decrease, and from decrease to increase, except the Lord of the Universe. Indeed, He has always been and will always be One. He is the First before everything, and He is the Last as He has always been. The attributes and names do not differ for Him as they differ for others, like the human being who is at one time dust, at another time flesh, at another time blood, and at another time bones and decay. And like the date, which is at one time unripe (busr), at another time ripe (rutab), and at another time dried (tamr), so that names and attributes change for it. And Allah, the Mighty and High, is different from that. [This is the] Chapter on the meaning of the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The Rahman established Himself over the Throne.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'The Last' (Al-Akhir) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates 'Al-Akhir' not merely as temporal finality but as ontological permanence, contrasting God's unchanging essence with the transient, state-dependent nature of creation. This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological emphasis on divine simplicity (tawhid al-sifat), where attributes do not undergo the biological or physical mutations seen in entities like humans or dates, thereby affirming God's absolute independence from change.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (RA) said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Jabbar, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Fudayl ibn `Uthman, on the authority of Ibn Abu Ya`fur that

I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: He is the First and the Last, and said: “We understand the meaning of the First. However, we need you to explain to us the meaning of the Last.” Therefore, he (AS) explained, Verily, there is nothing that does not perish, go through changes, deteriorate, change color, change form, change quality, increase or decrease, except the Lord of the Universe. Verily, He has always been, and will always be Solitary. He is the First that existed before everything. And He is the Last that will exist forever. The attributes and adjectives applied to Him are invariable. This is unlike human beings who are subject to change. At one stage they were dust, at another they were flesh and blood, and finally, their mortal remains decompose. Human beings are like dates [balah], which are subject to stages, moving from unripe [busr] to ripe dates [rutab], and from ripe dates to dried dates [tamr]. When applied to others but Allah, names and adjectives are subject to change. Allah, the Mighty and High, differs from those.
